question: The political landscape in India fundamentally changed as a result of the fourth general election held in the year _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1961
1977
1967
1972
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1967

Explanation:
The fourth general election in India was held in the year 1967. This election fundamentally changed the political landscape as the Congress party lost power in several states and secured a reduced majority at the centre. It was the first time the dominance of Congress was seriously challenged. Non-Congress coalition governments were formed in many states, marking the beginning of coalition politics and the rise of regional parties in India. The election further contributed to political fragmentation and diversity.

☛ Which party faced a challenge in the fourth general election? → Congress
☛ What type of governments emerged after the 1967 election? → Coalition governments
☛ In which year did Congress first get a reduced majority at the centre? → 1967
☛ How many seats did Congress win in the fourth general election? → 283 (in Lok Sabha)

question: Provision for the Administration and Control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes is mentioned under which of the following schedules? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sixth Schedule, Part A
Sixth Schedule, Part B
Fifth Schedule, Part B
Fifth Schedule, Part A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifth Schedule, Part A

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. This schedule is divided into Part A and Part B. Part A contains general provisions relating to the administration of Scheduled Areas, while Part B details the powers of the Union and States in administering these areas. This schedule is primarily applied under Article 244(1) and ensures special administrative arrangements for the development and protection of the interests of tribal communities in these areas. The Sixth Schedule, on the other hand, deals with the administration of tribal areas in the northeastern states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

☛ Which Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes? → Fifth Schedule
☛ What is in Part A of the Fifth Schedule? → General provisions for administration of Scheduled Areas
☛ What is in Part B of the Fifth Schedule? → Powers of Union and States
☛ Which states are covered under the Sixth Schedule? → Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram
question_hi: अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन और नियंत्रण का प्रावधान निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुसूची के अंतर्गत उल्लिखित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)

छठी अनुसूची, भाग बी
पांचवीं अनुसूची, भाग बी
पांचवीं अनुसूची, भाग ए
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पांचवीं अनुसूची, भाग ए

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की पांचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन और नियंत्रण का प्रावधान करती है। यह अनुसूची भाग ए और भाग बी में विभाजित है। भाग ए में अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से संबंधित सामान्य प्रावधान हैं, जबकि भाग बी में इन क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन में संघ और राज्यों की शक्तियों का उल्लेख है। यह अनुसूची मुख्य रूप से अनुच्छेद 244(1) के तहत लागू होती है और इन क्षेत्रों के विकास एवं जनजातीय समुदायों के हितों की रक्षा के लिए विशेष प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था सुनिश्चित करती है। छठी अनुसूची पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों में जनजातीय क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है।

question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution contains Articles 239 to 241 that deals with union territories? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Part X
Part VII
Part IX
Part VIII
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part VIII

Explanation:
Part VIII of the Indian Constitution, comprising Articles 239 to 242, deals with union territories. It lays down provisions for the administration of union territories, appointment of administrators (Lieutenant Governor or Administrator), and the formation of legislative assemblies or councils. Article 239 provides that each union territory shall be administered by the President through an administrator. Article 240 empowers the President to make regulations for certain union territories. Article 241 establishes High Courts for union territories. Other parts like Part X deals with scheduled tribes, Part VII (repealed), and Part IX deals with panchayats. Hence, the correct part for union territories is Part VIII.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article provides for administration of union territories? → Article 239
☛ Which article empowers President to make regulations for union territories? → Article 240
☛ Which article provides for High Courts in union territories? → Article 241
☛ Which part of Constitution contains union territories? → Part VIII
☛ Articles 239 to 241 belong to which part? → Part VIII
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भाग अनुच्छेद 239 से 241 से संबंधित है जो केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: भाग X
भाग VII
भाग IX
भाग VIII
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग VIII

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग VIII अनुच्छेद 239 से 242 तक केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से संबंधित है। यह भाग केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन, राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति, और विधान सभा के गठन जैसे प्रावधानों को निर्धारित करता है। अनुच्छेद 239 में प्रत्येक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का प्रशासन राष्ट्रपति द्वारा किया जाना प्रावधानित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 240 में कुछ केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के लिए नियम बनाने की शक्ति दी गई है। अनुच्छेद 241 में उच्च न्यायालयों का प्रावधान है। भाग X अनुसूचित जनजातियों से, भाग VII (निरस्त) और भाग IX पंचायतों से संबंधित है। इस प्रकार केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों का प्रावधान भाग VIII में है।

question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of recognised languages in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Eighth Schedule
Ninth Schedule
Tenth Schedule
Eleventh Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eighth Schedule

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of recognised languages. Originally it had 14 languages, which have been increased to 22 languages through amendments. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967), Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali by the 71st Amendment (1992), and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment (2003). These languages are important for official language commissions, parliamentary committees and government use. They include Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Kashmiri, etc. The schedule also influences the language policies of the Union and states.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule? → 22
☛ Which amendment added Sindhi? → 21st Amendment, 1967
☛ Which amendment added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali? → 71st Amendment, 1992
☛ Which amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali? → 92nd Amendment, 2003
☛ Which language in the Eighth Schedule is also a classical language? → Tamil

question: ‘Providing early childhood care and education to all children until they complete the age of 6 years’ belongs to which Section of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Fundamental Rights
Fundamental Duties
Legal responsibilities
Directive Principles of State Policy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution's Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). Article 45 directs the State to provide early childhood care and education to all children until they complete the age of 6 years. This is a directive principle, non-justiciable but fundamental in governance. The 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A, and amended Article 45 for children up to 6 years. DPSP aims to establish socio-economic justice, and Article 45 specifically focuses on early childhood care. These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and guide the State in policy-making.

☛ Part IV → Directive Principles of State Policy
☛ 86th Amendment → Made education a Fundamental Right, added Article 21A

☛ Source of Article 45 → Inspired by the Irish Constitution
question_hi: ‘सभी बच्चों को 6 वर्ष की आयु पूरी होने तक प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा प्रदान करना’ भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुभाग से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: मौलिक अधिकार
मौलिक कर्तव्य
कानूनी जिम्मेदारियां
राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत (DPSP) शामिल हैं। अनुच्छेद 45 के अनुसार, राज्य सभी बच्चों को 6 वर्ष की आयु पूरी होने तक प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा प्रदान करने का प्रयास करेगा। यह एक निदेशक सिद्धांत है, जो न्यायोचित नहीं है लेकिन देश के शासन में मौलिक है। 86वें संशोधन (2002) के बाद अनुच्छेद 21A में शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाया गया, जबकि अनुच्छेद 45 को 6 वर्ष तक के बच्चों के लिए संशोधित किया गया। DPSP का उद्देश्य सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करना है, और यह अनुच्छेद 45 बाल्यावस्था देखभाल पर केंद्रित है।

question: __________ has the power to amend the Constitution of India. (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Election Commission of India
The Prime Minister of India
The President of India
The Parliament of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Parliament of India

Explanation:
The power to amend the Constitution of India rests with the Parliament. This power is outlined in Article 368 of the Constitution. An amendment bill must be passed by both houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) with a special majority. For certain amendments affecting the federal structure, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures is also required. The President gives assent to the amendment bill but does not have the power to propose amendments. Thus, Parliament holds the primary authority in the amendment process.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who has the power to amend the Constitution? → The Parliament
☛ Which article deals with the amendment process? → Article 368
☛ What majority is required for an amendment bill? → Special majority
☛ When is state ratification required? → For amendments related to federal structure
☛ What is the President's role? → To give assent to the amendment bill
question_hi: __________ के पास भारत के संविधान में संशोधन करने की शक्ति है। (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: भारत का चुनाव आयोग
भारत के प्रधान मंत्री
भारत के राष्ट्रपति
भारत की संसद
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत की संसद

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान में संशोधन करने की शक्ति संसद को प्रदान की गई है। यह शक्ति संविधान के अनुच्छेद 368 में वर्णित है। संसद द्वारा संशोधन विधेयक को दोनों सदनों (लोकसभा और राज्यसभा) में विशेष बहुमत से पारित किया जाता है। कुछ संशोधनों के लिए राज्यों के आधे से अधिक विधानमंडलों की स्वीकृति भी आवश्यक होती है। राष्ट्रपति संशोधन विधेयक पर अपनी स्वीकृति देते हैं, लेकिन वह स्वयं संशोधन का प्रस्ताव नहीं कर सकते। इस प्रकार, संशोधन की प्रक्रिया में संसद की भूमिका सर्वोपरि है।

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts provides free legal aid as a Directive Principle of State Policy? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
46th Constitutional Amendment Act
86th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 brought several significant changes to the Indian Constitution. It added Article 39A to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which directs the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and to provide free legal aid to ensure that no citizen is denied opportunities for securing justice due to economic or other disabilities. This amendment is also known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made extensive changes, including adding the words socialist, secular, and integrity to the Preamble. It also added the Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. The 42nd Amendment was enacted during the Emergency period and aimed at strengthening the central government.

question: Under which Act is the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) constituted? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)

The Companies Act, 2013
solution:

Explanation:
The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) was constituted under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013. It is an appellate body that hears appeals against orders of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). Additionally, NCLAT hears appeals under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. question: Which of the following Acts had provided the establishment of a public service commission for recruiting civil servants in British India? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1929
Government of India Act, 1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of a Public Service Commission for recruiting civil servants in British India. This Act was based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms and introduced a system of diarchy at the provincial level. It also created a central Public Service Commission to oversee the recruitment of civil servants. Although the Act of 1919 laid the foundation, the actual commission was established in 1926, which later evolved into the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). The Act of 1935 further expanded and strengthened the commission's role. Thus, the 1919 Act was the first to envision a separate body for civil service recruitment.

question: Which Supreme Court case introduced the ‘basic structure’ doctrine in Indian Constitutional law? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Golaknath case 1967
Kesavananda Bharati case 1973
Minerva Mills case 1980
The Shankari Prasad case 1951
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesavananda Bharati case 1973

Explanation:
The 'basic structure' doctrine in Indian Constitutional law was introduced by the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973). A 13-judge Constitution bench ruled by a 7:6 majority that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its 'basic structure'. This doctrine limited Parliament's amending power. The Golaknath case (1967) had held that amendments are 'laws' and cannot affect Fundamental Rights. The Shankari Prasad case (1951) had stated that amending power is unlimited. The Minerva Mills case (1980) strengthened the basic structure doctrine, holding that Parliament cannot destroy Fundamental Rights.

☛ Number of judges in Kesavananda Bharati case? → 13-judge bench
☛ What did Golaknath case hold? → Amendments are 'laws'
☛ What did Minerva Mills case establish? → Basic structure and Fundamental Rights protection
☛ Shankari Prasad case's decision? → Amending power is unlimited

question: Which of the following Acts ended the company rule in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Indian Councils Act, 1892
Indian Councils Act, 1861
Government of India Act, 1858
Charter Act, 1853
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the rule of the British East India Company and transferred the governance of India directly to the British Crown. This act is also known as the 'Act for the Better Government of India'. It replaced the position of Governor-General with that of Viceroy, and Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. The act abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors, and established the Council of India headed by the Secretary of State. This act was passed after the Revolt of 1857, with the aim of establishing direct control of the British government over India.

question: What was a major focus of the 61st Constitutional Amendment? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Introduction of Anti-Defection Law
Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats
Abolition of Privy Purses for former rulers
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years

Explanation:
The 61st Constitutional Amendment (1989) primarily focused on lowering the voting age. It amended Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, reducing the minimum voting age for Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years. The amendment aimed to involve the youth in the political process, as 18 is considered the age of adulthood. This increased youth participation and strengthened democracy. Other options, such as the Anti-Defection Law (52nd Amendment), reservation of seats for women in Panchayats (73rd Amendment), and abolition of Privy Purses (26th Amendment), are related to different amendments.

भारत के विभाजन के समय, वर्तमान ओडिशा क्षेत्र में 26 छोटी रियासतें थीं जिन्हें भारतीय संघ में एकीकृत किया गया। ये रियासतें ब्रिटिश शासन के अधीन नहीं थीं, बल्कि स्थानीय शासकों द्वारा शासित थीं। 1947 में स्वतंत्रता के बाद, सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल के नेतृत्व में इन रियासतों का भारत में विलय हुआ। ओडिशा राज्य का गठन 1 अप्रैल 1936 को हुआ था, लेकिन विभाजन के बाद इन 26 रियासतों को मिलाकर ओडिशा का वर्तमान स्वरूप बना। यह प्रक्रिया भारतीय एकीकरण का महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा थी।

question: Protection of environment and wildlife is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 48A
Article 48
Article 47
Article 49
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 48A

Explanation:
The protection of environment and wildlife is mentioned under Article 48A of the Indian Constitution. This article was added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976. It directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife. Under the same amendment, Article 51A(g) was added as a fundamental duty of citizens to protect the environment. Article 48A is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which are non-justiciable but act as guiding principles for governance. The Supreme Court has used Article 48A to interpret environmental laws strictly and expand the scope of the right to life under Article 21.

question: What legal document allowed Princely States to join either India or Pakistan after independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Instrument of Accession
Standstill Agreement
Treaty of Accession
Pact of Unity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Instrument of Accession

Explanation:
Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, princely states were given the choice to join either India or Pakistan by signing the Instrument of Accession. This legal document allowed a state to accede to the dominion, surrendering control over only three subjects: defence, foreign affairs, and communications. The Instrument of Accession was the basis for the political integration of India, led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Most states signed it voluntarily, though some like Junagadh and Hyderabad had to be merged later. The process ensured India's territorial integrity.

☛ Who played the key role in integrating princely states? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Which three subjects were covered in the Instrument of Accession? → Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications
☛ Which princely state signed the first Instrument of Accession? → Bilaspur (October 1947)
☛ Which state acceded later due to special circumstances? → Jammu and Kashmir (26 October 1947)
